name: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (PALM-COEIN Classification and Management)

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / FIGO Menstrual Disorders Working Group
clinicalPearls: FIGO PALM-COEIN system classifies AUB into structural PALM and non-structural COEIN etiologies
Endometrial biopsy is mandatory in women aged 45 and older presenting with AUB, or younger with obesity and unopposed estrogen
Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (52 mg LNG-IUS) is the most effective first-line medical therapy for heavy bleeding
Tranexamic acid antifibrinolytic reduces menstrual blood loss by forty to fifty percent taken during bleeding days only
Atypical endometrial hyperplasia carries a concurrent forty percent risk of co-existing well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma
reference.pathophysiology: Normal menstruation relies on precise progesterone withdrawal triggering matrix metalloproteinase activation, spiral arteriolar vasoconstriction, and uniform endometrial sloughing. Structural lesions (polyps, adenomyosis, leiomyomas) disrupt mechanical vascular contractility and increase bleeding surface area. Non-structural causes involve coagulopathies, anovulatory progesterone deficiency, or primary endometrial dysregulation of endothelin and prostaglandins.
additionalDifferentials: Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia versus adenocarcinoma
Anovulatory AUB versus von Willebrand disease
additionalInvestigations: Transvaginal pelvic ultrasound to assess endometrial thickness and focal lesions
Saline infusion sonohysterography or diagnostic hysteroscopy
